content.text: {"label":"unknown_supply_issue","explanation":"Demand does not explain the shortfall. Payments volume is 12% below forecast today, and general volume is only 2% above forecast overall, though it has risen 13–23% in recent intervals. The main problem is staffing. Payments has 46 agents against 62.4 expected, and general has 30 against 35.5. Attendance shows 19 and 11 absences, against a usual 2–3 per day. Most of these are lateness logged as 'Bus strike - unable to reach office' (14 and 8), with only 5 and 3 sick calls, so this is not a sick wave. No live incident or system problem accounts for it: the only incident is a resolved overnight batch. The social fraud post shows no fraud-call spike. Of the allowed labels, an external supply disruption fits best. General is hurting most: service level was 26.9% at 15:15, with 31 agents on phones against about 30 Erlangs of load. Payments is borderline at 77%.","plan_name":"Late-day general recovery under bus-strike absence","rationale":"General needs about 4–5 more productive agents. Payments cannot donate agents: at about 28 Erlangs on 31 agents it would likely fall below 70%, so no cross-skill move is made. Most of the overtime budget is already used: about Rs 13,250 of Rs 15,000 committed, assuming 40% acceptance. So one small general overtime offer stays within the remaining roughly Rs 1,750 (about 1.6 accepted agents x 2 h x Rs 360 ≈ Rs 1,150). The free and cheap levers carry the rest. Cancelling coaching on both queues returns agents to the phones. Delaying general breaks in the next two hours borrows capacity; agents already delayed today are skipped, so the effect is limited. Callbacks on both queues smooth the peaks. Chat deflection on general targets balance_enquiry, the fastest-rising eligible reason, plus new_offer_enquiry.
